question: Is it permissible if I do not know where the impurity is, but know the trousers are impure to just clean where the impurity has ‘probably’ befallen.
title: Is it permissible if I do not know where the impurity is, but know the trousers are impure to just clean where the impurity has ‘probably’ befallen.
answer:
ANSWER:
If you are certain that there is a najasah but you don’t know where, some scholars say it is sufficient to wash the area most likely you believe the najasah is at. Other scholars say that you need to wash the whole trousers and I am inclined to this opinion.

title: Missed 2 rak with d imam,I joined him whn he ws sayin d takbeer 2 rise 2 d 3rd rak,then I thot mybe he was not erect nd I ws standin(standin before he stood),so I broke my pryr,then started again nd I didnt complete my fatihah and he said takbeer(fearin not completin the fatihah) I broke my pryr again nd joined him again nd continued my pryr. Wht shud b done here nd is my pryr vld
answer:
ANSWER:

question: I came across a statement attributed to Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn in [Tafsir Sūrat al-Mā’idah by Sheikh Ibn ʿUthaymin p.403] indicating that one who abandons prayer or commits clear acts of kufr is treated and even declared a disbeliever by name outwardly. However, in other places he states that takfīr of a specific individual requires establishing proof. and how are these statements reconciled?
title: I came across a statement attributed to Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn in [Tafsir Sūrat al-Mā’idah by Sheikh Ibn ʿUthaymin p.403] indicating that one who abandons prayer or commits clear acts of kufr is treated and even declared a disbeliever by name outwardly. However, in other places he states that takfīr of a specific individual requires establishing proof. and how are these statements reconciled?
answer:
ANSWER:
There are theoretical aspects of it and practical aspects.
The first opinion is the theoretical part which is a generic statement: any one who doesn’t pray is a kafir.
The second statement is the practical part which is that we can’t label specific individual with kufr until the conditions are fulfilled and obstacles are eliminated.

question: When one forgets a pillar of prayer, for example the ruku in the first rakat and one remembers it after finishing the prayer, what should one do in this situation?
title: When one forgets a pillar of prayer, for example the ruku in the first rakat and one remembers it after finishing the prayer, what should one do in this situation?
answer:
ANSWER:
If he remembers immediately after finishing, he must stand up and offer one more rakah as his first whole rakah was invalid due to missing pillar. 
So he stands up, recites the fatiha, makes ruku and two prostrations and then sits for final tashahud, offers salam, then offers 2 prostrations of forgetfulness and then offer the last salam.

question: It happens I pray 3times in different mosques. How many times do I pray tahiyat masjid?
title: It happens I pray 3times in different mosques. How many times do I pray tahiyat masjid?

Everytime you enter the masjid, you must pray before sitting down, it can be any prayer, whether 2 specific rakahs of tahiyatul masjid, sunnah before the obligatory prayer or fard prayer itself. question: My bus in the morning picks me up before athan so I can not pray at home and i am going to a non muslim school, so I pray on the bus, is this permissible?
title: My bus in the morning picks me up before athan so I can not pray at home and i am going to a non muslim school, so I pray on the bus, is this permissible?
answer:
ANSWER:
It is permissible to pray anywhere when the prayer is due. However, one must fulfill the conditions of prayer such as facing the Qibla. therefore, if a person is on a bus, he must face the Qibla, but if he is unable, then he can start his prayer facing the Qibla and then it is Ok to face anywhere else as long as this is not possible. He also must pray standing up as this is a pillar of the prayer. if he is unable at all to stand –and this is hypothetical- he may pray sitting down. If he is able to get off the bus, he should so that he can pray in the normal way.

When I finally woke up I prayed the missed fajr prayer. Also this is not something that happens regularly since I basically never miss the fajr prayer and always hear my fajr alarm.

question: In urine incontinence, as the wudu breaks after ending time. Can I pray 2 rakah nafl after the time has passed (of dhuhr 12 rakahs) or I am obliged to pray nafl (10-12th rakah) after renewing wudu
title: In urine incontinence, as the wudu breaks after ending time. Can I pray 2 rakah nafl after the time has passed (of dhuhr 12 rakahs) or I am obliged to pray nafl (10-12th rakah) after renewing wudu
answer:
ANSWER:
There are no 12 rakahs for dhuhr. 
Dhuhr is only 4 rakahs and the emphatic sunnah (which is highly recommended but not mandatory) are 4 (2×2) before fard and 2 after fard. If you missed these sunnah prayers until the time of asr was due, you need to renew your wudhu to make them up.

question: I joined the imam in the 2nd rakah of maghrib. He thought it was his last and was about to make Salam but people corrected him. He then prayed the third rakah and performed sajd e sahu. Should I also perform sajd e sahu or not as it is my 2nd rakah.
title: I joined the imam in the 2nd rakah of maghrib. He thought it was his last and was about to make Salam but people corrected him. He then prayed the third rakah and performed sajd e sahu. Should I also perform sajd e sahu or not as it is my 2nd rakah.
answer:
ANSWER:
If he performed it before the salam, you must offer it with him as well. But if he performed it after the salam, you don’t offer it with him as you must stand up to make up your missed rakah and then complete your prayer as usual.

question: One day while praying ‘Asr in the mosque, the Imam mistakenly sat in the 3rd rakah and recited Tashahhud. I initially got up and stood but later sat down again when I saw that the Imam did not rise up for the “4th rakah” but I did not recite the tashahhud in the 3rd rakah like the Imam. The Imam along with everyone of us offered sujood-as-sahw before concluding the prayer. Did I do anything wrong?
title: One day while praying ‘Asr in the mosque, the Imam mistakenly sat in the 3rd rakah and recited Tashahhud. I initially got up and stood but later sat down again when I saw that the Imam did not rise up for the “4th rakah” but I did not recite the tashahhud in the 3rd rakah like the Imam. The Imam along with everyone of us offered sujood-as-sahw before concluding the prayer. Did I do anything wrong?
answer:
ANSWER:
If the imam sat mistakenly in the 3rd, you should notify him by saying subhana Allah 
If he doesn’t listen and rectify his mistake by standing up to the 4th, you must leave him and stand up to your fourth and finish you prayer alone.
It is not permissible to follow him in that as it is not permissible to follow him if he were to stand up to the 5th rakah for example.
The prayer is invalid for dropping a whole rakah and that can’t be compensated by sujood  assahu.

question: I am to catch a flight soon and I’m worried about not being able to pray esha on time. Can I combine and pray esha  at maghrib time? Similarly on my way to the airport there is a risk of not being able to pray asr on time, again can I pray asr at zuhr time and combine?  Also upon reaching destination I will be there for 7/8 days can I combine prayers while I am there for those 7/8 days
title: I am to catch a flight soon and I’m worried about not being able to pray esha on time. Can I combine and pray esha  at maghrib time? Similarly on my way to the airport there is a risk of not being able to pray asr on time, again can I pray asr at zuhr time and combine?  Also upon reaching destination I will be there for 7/8 days can I combine prayers while I am there for those 7/8 days
answer:

question: Can I recite dua after adhan when it’s time for adhan but I can’t hear it due to rain? Will it be bidah if I do it?

answer:
The sunnah is to repeat after a live athaan and say the dua after hearing it. If you can’t hear it, you shouldn’t say the duaa. If you are a male, you can call the athan yourself and say the duaa.

question: My menses start at the end of each month (or one day or two before or after). It starts with pink/red discharges and then after a few hours or after a day I see the flow of blood. The ending of my menses is the same. After about four days of flowing blood, I see spotting and then in one day, I am pure. Are the spots in my case considered part of my period and I should stop praying/fasting?
title: My menses start at the end of each month (or one day or two before or after). It starts with pink/red discharges and then after a few hours or after a day I see the flow of blood. The ending of my menses is the same. After about four days of flowing blood, I see spotting and then in one day, I am pure. Are the spots in my case considered part of my period and I should stop praying/fasting?
answer: You must disregard any spotting that come before the period. It is not your menstruation until you see the flow of blood and you must not stop praying, fasting and you can have intimacy with your husband during these spotting. You must wash the affected areas, change the underwear and renew your wudu before praying.If the flow of blood stops at the end of your menses and you see dryness for one day, take your ghusul and pray. The spotting afterwards only invalidates your wudhu but this is not menses as it comes after your purity. Purity is identified by seeing a white thread like discharge or by experiencing complete dryness. question: Does only all the redness in the sky have to disappear for Isha time? In high latitude areas, looking outside the sky’s dark with stars visible but north of the sky isn’t (has lightness & appears light blue). Masjid has Isha time about 1 hour after Maghrib (earlier than Um al Qura) but sky appears as described & ISNA is later than UaQ & MWL is about 2 hours later – any advise on which to follow?
title: Does only all the redness in the sky have to disappear for Isha time? In high latitude areas, looking outside the sky’s dark with stars visible but north of the sky isn’t (has lightness & appears light blue). Masjid has Isha time about 1 hour after Maghrib (earlier than Um al Qura) but sky appears as described & ISNA is later than UaQ & MWL is about 2 hours later – any advise on which to follow?
answer: You need to check with your scholars in your country. What I believe is that if there is redness towards the west, isha time begins when it disappears.But if there is no redness and it is only whiteness and brightness, one should refer to the nearest country that has redness and follows them in regards to their isha time beginning. Does only all the redness in the sky have to disappear for Isha time? question: What is the ruling on someone who goes to perform umrah and then made intention to be in the state of ihram and to perform umrah but he wasn’t wearing the ihram while making the intention and then change his mind and decided to not perform umrah and return to his country (can he cancel his intention?)
title: What is the ruling on someone who goes to perform umrah and then made intention to be in the state of ihram and to perform umrah but he wasn’t wearing the ihram while making the intention and then change his mind and decided to not perform umrah and return to his country (can he cancel his intention?)
answer:
ANSWER:
It seems that you don’t know what it means to be in the state of Ihram.
The intention to make an Umrah is different from intending to assume the state of Ihram.
To assume the state of Ihram, one must put on the ihram towels, firmly intend after this point not to do any of the restricted acts of ihram such as wearing perfumes, clipping nails etc.
This is where he can’t simply change his mind.
But to have the intention to make umrah without assuming the state of Ihram and then changing your mind, this is permissible and no problem in doing that.
                
                QUESTION: What is the ruling on someone who goes to perform umrah and then made intention to be in the state of ihram and to perform umrah but he wasn’t wearing the ihram while making the intention and then change his mind and decided to not perform umrah and return to his country (can he cancel his intention?)

question: If I give Zakath to a person and that person distributes it on monthly basis, is this permissible ?
title: If I give Zakath to a person and that person distributes it on monthly basis, is this permissible ?
answer:
ANSWER:
No, this is not permissible.
You must instruct him to give it away to poor and needy Muslims on the day your zakat is due (a few days of delay is fine, but not more than that)
If you want to give it on a monthly basis you can give next year’s zakat in advance

question: Does zakat apply to women’s own earnings?
title: Does zakat apply to women’s own earnings?
answer:

question: Sheikh if calculate the zakat on my gold on say Nov 1st but I don’t have the money to pay off all my zakat all at once and I would need to pay it off in installments, do I hold to that one calculation from Nov 1st until I pay it all off or do I recalculate with the gold price for Dec 1st when I’m paying off the next installment?
title: Sheikh if calculate the zakat on my gold on say Nov 1st but I don’t have the money to pay off all my zakat all at once and I would need to pay it off in installments, do I hold to that one calculation from Nov 1st until I pay it all off or do I recalculate with the gold price for Dec 1st when I’m paying off the next installment?

ANSWER:
Its not permissible to pay the zakat on instalments! You must pay it on the due date (hijri Islamic calendar), can take a couple of days extra but CANNOT delay it much further!
Sell some of your gold to pay the zakat on time if you don’t have the cash

question: There is a poor cousin of mine who got her leg fractured so can i keep a house help at her house and pay off her salary from my zakat

question: My gold doesn’t exceed the threshold amount of zakat. If I mix them with cash then the amount exceeds the zakat threshold of silver. Can I give zakat based on this calculation? or should I calculate based on only cash?
title: My gold doesn’t exceed the threshold amount of zakat. If I mix them with cash then the amount exceeds the zakat threshold of silver. Can I give zakat based on this calculation? or should I calculate based on only cash?
answer:
ANSWER:
If you have cash that would mount to the thresh hold of gold when added to the gold you have, you should give zakat. 
But if it doesn’t reach the threshold of gold but the cash is above the threshold of silver, you must give zakat only on the cash and not the gold.

title: Two years ago I lent my mom some money(which is above Nisab amount), with the idea that she would pay it back when she was able to. Yes, you should pay the zakat for the past 2 years.

question: I’ve had money over the nisab for nearly a year so I know I have to pay 2.5% of that. But I’m confused about what to do with any new gifted money I may get. This money isn’t over the nisab and I spend it sometimes so if I get different amounts on different dates how do I work out the zakaah? If it totals up to the nisab after a few months do I start counting a year from then?
title: I’ve had money over the nisab for nearly a year so I know I have to pay 2.5% of that. But I’m confused about what to do with any new gifted money I may get. This money isn’t over the nisab and I spend it sometimes so if I get different amounts on different dates how do I work out the zakaah? If it totals up to the nisab after a few months do I start counting a year from then?
answer: It is very difficult to calculate the zakat every month when money is coming at different times. This is why it is best and safest to assign one day in the year and on that day, we calculate all the wealth we have in our possession whether it came a year ago or a month ago and give 2.5% and not bother with zakat until the following year. I’ve had money over the nisab for nearly a year so I know I have to pay 2.5% of that. question: I have appx 150g of Gold. My husband is giving zakah on it on my behalf from past few years as we don’t want to sell gold. My question is that we have to continuously give zakah every year like this if we don’t want to sell gold? Also my daughter is three year old and she received gold gifts, do I need to include her gold in mine to calculate my zakah?
title: I have appx 150g of Gold. My husband is giving zakah on it on my behalf from past few years as we don’t want to sell gold. My question is that we have to continuously give zakah every year like this if we don’t want to sell gold? Also my daughter is three year old and she received gold gifts, do I need to include her gold in mine to calculate my zakah?
answer:
1. Yes, zakat must be given every year if it stays with you. 2. No, her zakat should be calculated separately if it reaches nisab, which is 85 grams.

question: Firstly thank u so much for replying my queries, Allah bless you.I heard that condition of paying zakat is the custody of amount 1 lunar year.like in last Ramadan I had 1lakh and in this ramzan few months back I collected some amount and now is 1.4 lakh ,so I will pay zakah on 1lakh as this amount I had for whole year.Am I right?
title: Firstly thank u so much for replying my queries, Allah bless you.I heard that condition of paying zakat is the custody of amount 1 lunar year.like in last Ramadan I had 1lakh and in this ramzan few months back I collected some amount and now is 1.4 lakh ,so I will pay zakah on 1lakh as this amount I had for whole year.Am I right?
answer:
You pay the zakat over what a full lunar year finished which is the one lakh.
However, it is best if you unite the date for all what you have whether it came a year ago or few months ago as keeping track with which came when is difficult if not impossible.

question: Shiekh how to calculate unpaid zakaat on gold where the date of purchasing is not known and its purchased on different dates. What if the zakaat is more than my income, can I pay from my monthly salary for 1 or 2 years every month. Can it be given to same person every month?
title: Shiekh how to calculate unpaid zakaat on gold where the date of purchasing is not known and its purchased on different dates. What if the zakaat is more than my income, can I pay from my monthly salary for 1 or 2 years every month. Can it be given to same person every month?
answer:
You must estimate on the date and pay zakat on every year that you’ve had it in your possession for over one lunar year if it reached the nisab level. It must be given to a poor and needy Muslim in the form of cash. If you don’t have cash to pay it, you must sell some of the gold.

question: I have couple family members whom I give zakah money every month. I pay let’s say my 2.5 % of wealth will be $6,000 I pay according to that and I can’t wait till end of the year to give them zakat money because they need money every month to survive so is it ok for me to give them money every month instead of waiting till end of year because they need it.
title: I have couple family members whom I give zakah money every month. I pay let’s say my 2.5 % of wealth will be $6,000 I pay according to that and I can’t wait till end of the year to give them zakat money because they need money every month to survive so is it ok for me to give them money every month instead of waiting till end of year because they need it.
answer:
Last year’s zakat must be paid immediately once it is due. You can’t give
it in installments.
However, you can estimate next year’s zakat and give it on monthly basis
and once the date is due, you calculate how much you gave and if there is a
balance left, give it on the spot.

question: I forgot to pay Fitrana before Eid prayers. What can i do now?
title: I forgot to pay Fitrana before Eid prayers. What can i do now?
answer:
Praise be to Allaah.There is no sin on him because he is excused for his forgetfulness, but he has to pay it when he remembers it.
Shaykh ‘Abd al-‘Azeez ibn Baaz (may Allah have mercy on him) was asked about someone who forgot to pay zakaat al-fitr on time, and he replied:
There is no doubt that the Sunnah is to pay zakaat al-fitr before the Eid prayer, as enjoined by the Prophet (blessings and peace of Allah be upon), but there is nothing wrong with what you did; paying it after the prayer is acceptable, praise be to Allah. Even though it says in the hadeeth that it is ordinary charity, that does not necessarily mean that it is not valid and was not done appropriately. So we hope that it will be acceptable and be regarded as proper zakaah, because you did not delay it deliberately; rather you delayed it because you forgot, and Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, says in His Book (interpretation of the meaning): “Our Lord! Punish us not if we forget or fall into error” [al-Baqarah 2:286]. And it is proven that the Prophet (blessings and peace of Allah be upon him) said: “Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, says: I will do that.” So He has answered the prayer of His believing slave not to punish them if they forget or fall into error.
End quote from Majmoo‘ Fataawa al-Shaykh Ibn Baaz, 14/217
Shaykh Ibn ‘Uthaymeen (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Whoever pays it before the prayer, it is valid zakaah, and whoever  pays it after the prayer, it is ordinary charity”– unless the individual is excused, such as if he forgot to pay it and did not remember it until after the prayer, or he had intended to give it to the one who usually gives it on his behalf, then after that he found out that his deputy had not paid it, so he pays it himself, or if he found out that it was Eid too late, then he pays it after the prayer. title: I have given five hunderd thausand (500000)doller on loan to four(4) deffrint people i have been giving zakat for the last four years and still i am not sure when they are going return me the money or even i am not sure if they are going to give me all my money so now should i wait till i get money and then give ZAKAT or should i keep giving ZAKAT.

If you ask them for the money every year and insist on getting it back and they apologize that they don’t have or refuse to give it back, there is no zakat on it until you receive it!

question: My question is can u plz explain which ppl deserve zakat?
title: My question is can u plz explain which ppl deserve zakat?
answer:
Praise be to Allaah.There are eight categories on which zakaah must be spent, which Allaah has explained clearly. He states that this is a duty imposed by Allaah and that it is based on knowledge and wisdom. Allaah, may He be exalted, says (interpretation of the meaning):
“As-Sadaqaat (here it means Zakaah) are only for the Fuqaraa’ (poor), and Al‑Masaakeen (the poor) and those employed to collect (the funds); and to attract the hearts of those who have been inclined (towards Islam); and to free the captives; and for those in debt; and for Allaah’s Cause (i.e. for Mujaahidoon — those fighting in a holy battle), and for the wayfarer (a traveller who is cut off from everything); a duty imposed by Allaah. And Allaah is All-Knower, All-Wise”
[al-Tawbah 9:60]
These eight are the categories who are entitled to zakaah and to whom it must be paid.
The first and second are the fuqara’ and masaakeen (the poor and needy). They should be given zakaah to meet their needs. The difference between the fuqara’ and masaakeen is that the fuqara’ are in greater need; one of them cannot find enough to suffice himself and his dependents for half a year. The masaakeen are better off than the fuqara’, because they can find half of what will suffice them or more. These people should be given zakaah because of their need.
But how can we evaluate need?
The scholars said: They should be given what they need to suffice them and their families for one year, because when the year has passed, zakaah will become due again. Just as the year is the unit of time by which zakaah becomes due, so too the year should be the unit of time by which the poor and needy, who are entitled to zakaah, should be given zakaah. This is a good view, i.e., we should give the poor and needy person what will suffice him and his family for a full year, whether we give it in the form of food and clothing, or we give him money with which to buy what suits him, or we give him tools with which he can make things, if

question: Dear Sheikh, I have a question about zakah:I have 200 grams gold and I am paying zakat from it.My friend says subtract nasab amount (96 grams) from your gold then pay zakah of it.Meaning, I should pay zakat from 104 grams (i.e. 2.6 grams).I hope you understand.
title: Dear Sheikh, I have a question about zakah:I have 200 grams gold and I am paying zakat from it.My friend says subtract nasab amount (96 grams) from your gold then pay zakah of it.Meaning, I should pay zakat from 104 grams (i.e. 2.6 grams).I hope you understand.
answer:

question: My brother is admitted in hospital due to psychiatric problem and he cannot pay his fees. Can I use my zakath amount to pay his monthly bills.
title: My brother is admitted in hospital due to psychiatric problem and he cannot pay his fees. Can I use my zakath amount to pay his monthly bills.
answer:
There are few issues here. If you are one of the heirs who would inherit him if he were to die, you must provide for him and can’t give him your zakat. But if his father is alive or he has a son, then you can give him from zakat.
He has to be poor or needy in order to qualify for being a recipient of zakat.
The zakat must of the previous year be given at once. However, you can give him from the zakat of the next year in installments until its due date.

question: I wantd To ask abt paying zakat this Ramadan. Say I have Rs 1lac in my account for less than a year.. Do I have to pay zakat for it?  And if I already had Rs 1lac in my account last year for which I already paid zakat in the month of Ramadan last year. Now this year one more lac got added to it but this lac was with me for less than a yr. do I have to pay zakat for 2lacs

Now this year one more lac got added to it but this lac was with me for less than a yr. do I have to pay zakat for 2lacs
answer:
Zakat is due on any savings that finishes one year in your possession.
It is best to designate a specific date every Hijra year and in that
day, calculate whatever savings you have and give zakat on it
regardless when it came into your possession.

question: Is it permissible to give zakat to more than one person? If Allah has given him plenty wealth and he is a billionaire, he then gives his zakat to 2 or more people. Maybe if given to one person can receive millions or close to, instead he gives to 2 or more if the money is plenty so they can benefit from it?
title: Is it permissible to give zakat to more than one person? If Allah has given him plenty wealth and he is a billionaire, he then gives his zakat to 2 or more people. Maybe if given to one person can receive millions or close to, instead he gives to 2 or more if the money is plenty so they can benefit from it?
answer:
One must not give his zakat to a person or more to the extent that they become rich! He should give the poor what suffices him for a year! Therefore, if his zakat is in millions, this should be given to thousands of people and not one or two. He should also be careful to whom he gives it to!

question: If you owe 2 houses, does zakat have to be paid on them both?

question: Can someone have multiple sacrifices in different countries?  For example: 2 in india, 1 in residing country?  Where 1 whole Indian goat goes to charity  The second for family and friends.
title: Can someone have multiple sacrifices in different countries?  For example: 2 in india, 1 in residing country?  Where 1 whole Indian goat goes to charity  The second for family and friends.
answer:
ANSWER:
This is permissible but it is not per the sunnah 
The sunnah is to divide each sacrifice into three parts 
If someone sacrificed 3 sheep, made one charity, one as a gift and the 3rd for himself to eat from, that is wrong!
The sunnah is to divide each sheep to three parts

question: I, my brother and his son living under one roof. my intention is for my deceased wife and son, can we share the cost and get one goat and have both our intentions?
title: I, my brother and his son living under one roof. my intention is for my deceased wife and son, can we share the cost and get one goat and have both our intentions?

question: My question is that when and till when should we recite taqbeer and what is the proper taqbeer?
title: My question is that when and till when should we recite taqbeer and what is the proper taqbeer?
answer:
First thirteen days of Dhul Hijjah.
Praise be to Allaah.  Firstly – The virtue of Takbeer
The first ten days of Dhu’l-Hijjah are venerated days. Allaah swore by them in His Book, and swearing by a thing is indicative of its importance and great benefit. Allaah says (interpretation of the meaning):
“By the dawn;
By the ten nights (i.e. the first ten days of the month of Dhul-Hijjah)”
[al-Fajr 89:1]
Ibn ‘Abbaas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Mujaahid and others among the earlier and later generations said: This refers to the ten days of Dhu’l-Hijjah. Ibn Katheer said: This is the correct view.
Tafseer Ibn Katheer, 8/413
Good deeds during these days are beloved to Allaah, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allaah than these ten days.” They said, “O Messenger of Allaah, not even jihad for the sake of Allaah?” The Messenger of Allaah (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said, “Not even jihad for the sake of Allaah, except in the case of a man who went out to fight, giving himself and his wealth up for the cause, and came back with nothing.” Narrated by al-Bukhaari, 969; al-Tirmidhi, 757. This version was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and classed as saheeh by al-Albaani in Saheeh al-Tirmidhi, 605.
One of the righteous deeds during these days is to remember Allaah by reciting takbeer (saying “Allaahu akbar”) and tahleel (saying “Laa ilaaha ill-Allaah”), because of the following evidence.
1 – Allaah says (interpretation of the meaning):
“That they may witness things that are of benefit to them (i.e. reward of Hajj in the Hereafter, and also some worldly gain from trade), and mention the Name of Allaah on appointed days”
[al-Hajj 22:28]
The “appointed days” are the first ten days of Dhu’l-Hijjah.
2 – Allaah says (interpretation of the meaning):
“And remember Allaah during the appointed Days”
[al-Baqarah 2:203]
These are the days of al-Tashreeq, i.e. the 11th, 12th and 13th of Dhu’l-Hijjah.
3 – The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “The days of tashreeq are the days of eating, drinking and remembering Allaah.” Narrated by Muslim, 1141.
Secondly: Description of the Takbeer
The scholars differed concerning the form of the Takbeer.
1 – The first view is that it is:
Allaahu akbar, Allaahu akbar, laa ilaaha ill-Allaah, Allaahu akbar, Allaahu akbar, wa lillaahi’l-hamd(Allaah is Most Great, Allaah is Most Great, there is no god but Allaah, Allaah is Most Great, Allaah is Most Great, and to Allaah be praise).
2 – The second view is that it is:
Allaahu akbar, Allaahu akbar, Allaahu akbar, laa ilaaha ill-Allaah, Allaahu akbar, Allaahu akbar, Allaahu akbar, wa lillaahi’l-hamd (Allaah is Most Great, Allaah is Most Great, Allaah is Most Great, there is no god but Allaah, Allaah is Most Great, Allaah is Most Great, Allaah is Most Great, and to Allaah be praise).
3 – The third view is that it is:
Allaahu akbar, Allaahu akbar, Allaahu akbar, laa ilaaha ill-Allaah,

question: Is it necessary that the animal of sacrifice should be of one year old or it could be of any age?  What are the requirements for an animal of sacrifice?
title: Is it necessary that the animal of sacrifice should be of one year old or it could be of any age?  What are the requirements for an animal of sacrifice?
answer:
The scholars (may Allaah have mercy on them) are agreed that Islam has prescribed the age for sacrificial animals and it is not permissible to slaughter animals that are younger than that. Whoever slaughters an animal that is younger than that, it does not count as a sacrifice.
See al-Majmoo’ by al-Nawawi, 1/176.
For example, al-Bukhaari (5556) and Muslim (1961) narrated that al-Bara’ ibn ‘Aazib (may Allaah have mercy on him) said: A maternal uncle of mine whose name was Abu Burdah slaughtered his sacrifice before the prayer, and the Messenger of Allaah (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said to him: “Your sheep is a sheep for meat (i.e., not a sacrifice).” He said: “O Messenger of Allaah, I have a young goat (according to another report: I have a young she-goat) (according to a report by al-Bukhaari (5563): I have a jadha’ah which is better than two musinnahs – shall I sacrifice it?)” The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “Sacrifice it, but that will not be valid for anyone but you.” According to another report: “It will not count for anyone after you.” Then he said: “Whoever slaughters (the animal) before the prayer has slaughtered it for himself, and whoever slaughters it after the prayer has offered the sacrifice and followed the way of the Muslims.”
This hadeeth indicates that a jadha’ah of goats (young goat) is not sufficient as a sacrifice. We will explain below what jadha’ah means.
Ibn al-Qayyim said in Tahdheeb al-Sunan:
The phrase “It will not count for anyone after you” is a definitive statement that it would not count for anyone after him. End quote.
Muslim (1963) narrated that Jaabir (may Allaah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allaah (peace and blessings of Allaah be upon him) said: “Do not slaughter anything but a musinnah, unless it is too hard for you, in which case you should slaughter a young sheep (jadha’ah min al-da’n).
This hadeeth also clearly states that only a musinnah can be slaughtered, except in the case of sheep, where a jadha’ah may be offered.
Al-Nawawi said in Sharh Muslim:
The scholars said:
A musinnah is a thaniyyah of anything, camel, cow or sheep, or anything over that age. This clearly indicates that it is not permissible to slaughter a jadha’ah of any animal in any circumstances, except sheep. End quote.
Al-Haafiz said in al-Talkhees, 4/285:
The apparent meaning of the hadeeth suggests that a jadha’ah of sheep is not permissible except if one cannot find a musinnah. Scholarly consensus says something different, so this hadeeth should be understood as referring to what is better. So it is mustahabb not to slaughter anything but a musinnah. End quote.
Al-Nawawi said in Sharh Muslim:
It says in ‘Awn al-Ma’bood:
This interpretation is the one which is correct. End quote.
Then he quoted some of the ahaadeeth which indicate that it is permissible to offer a jadha’ah of sheep as a sacrifice, such as the hadeeth of ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Aamir (may Allaah be pleased with him) who said

Giving udhiyah(qurbani)meat to Non Muslims is permissible, especially if they are your neighbors.

question: Other than sheep or goat is it ok to slaughter cow for the aqiqa of a new born baby? In that case should it also be 2 cow for a baby boy and 1 cow for baby girl?
title: Other than sheep or goat is it ok to slaughter cow for the aqiqa of a new born baby? In that case should it also be 2 cow for a baby boy and 1 cow for baby girl?
answer:
Praise be to Allah
Slaughtering a cow with the intention of some of it being for the ‘aqeeqah and some for the udhiyah is a matter concerning which the scholars differed. The Hanafis and Shaafa‘is regard it as permissible.
Ibn ‘Aabideen al-Hanafi said, concerning the permissibility of making a joint intention in such cases:
It is permissible regardless of whether the sacrifice is obligatory on all or some of them, and whether the reason for it is one reason or not, such as if the reason is as a sacrifice (udhiyah) or as a result of being prevented from proceeding to Makkah (after having entered ihram), or as a penalty for hunting game or for shaving (when in ihram), or because one is doing tamattu‘ (‘umrah followed by Hajj, exiting ihram in between) or qiraan (‘umrah followed by Hajj, without exiting ihram in between). This is different from the view of Zufr, because the aim in all cases is to draw closer to Allah. The same applies if the reason of some of them is to offer ‘aqeeqah for a child who was born before that, because the ‘aqeeqah is an act by which one intends to draw closer to Allah by showing gratitude for having a child.
In al-Fataawa al-Fiqhiyyah al-Kubra by Ibn Hajar al-Haytami ash-Shaafa‘i (4/256) it says:
If he slaughters a camel or a cow for seven reasons, including udhiyah and ‘aqeeqah, and the rest are expiations for things such as shaving whilst in ihram, that is acceptable, and it does not come under the heading of superimposition, because each of the seven parts of the camel or cow will be for a particular reason, and that is valid. End quote.
The Hanbalis disallowed making additional intentions when offering the ‘aqeeqah in all cases, so in their view it is not acceptable to slaughter a cow or camel unless it is all for one ‘aqeeqah, for one child. It says in Sharh Muntaha al-Iraadaat (1/614):
It is not acceptable to slaughter a camel or a cow for an ‘aqeeqah, unless the entire animal (is intended for that ‘aqeeqah). End quote.

question: Is it allowed to slaughter one goat or sheep for all family members during EID-Al-Adha? Can we include Mother, Father, Wife, Kids, sisters, brother and brother’s wife in one Goat or sheep?

question: I live in USA. We have some muslim brothers doing real estate business. They buy land or old houses and then built new homes and sell them . They have some investment options where if i give them some money they will give me a profit ranging from 25-27% but not fix after 1 year. My question is , is this sharia compliant way to invest my money?
title: I live in USA. We have some muslim brothers doing real estate business. They buy land or old houses and then built new homes and sell them . They have some investment options where if i give them some money they will give me a profit ranging from 25-27% but not fix after 1 year. My question is , is this sharia compliant way to invest my money?
answer: You need first to know what is the percentage of your investment from the whole capital so that when you want out, you can estimate the actual value of the establishment and estimate your own capital accordingly. There must be no guarantee that your capital investment is guaranteed back. question: One of the student of knowledge told me mufti taqi usmani is an expert in this and he is the highest ranked scholar in your country and that’s enough for am Aami to know. Below is the nature of their agreement Car Ijarah is Pakistan’s first Interest Free car financing based on the Islamic financing mode of Ijarah (Islamic leasing). This product is ideal for individuals looking for car financing while avoiding an interest-based transaction. Meezan Bank’ Car Ijarah is a car rental agreement, under which the  Bank purchases the car and rents it out to the customer for a period of 1 to 5 years, agreed at the time of the contract. Upon completion of the lease period the customer gets ownership of the car against his initial security deposit. An Islamic Ijarah is an asset-based contract, i.e. the Lessor should have ownership of the asset during the period of the contract. Under Islamic Shariah, all ownership related rights and liabilities should lie with the owner while all usage-related rights and liabilities should lie with the user. A conventional lease contract does not distinguish between the nature of these liabilities and places all liabilities on the user of the asset, which is contradictory to Islamic Shariah. Under Ijarah, all ownership-related risks lie with the Bank while all usage related risks lie with the user, thus making the Lessor the true owner of the asset and making the income generated through the contract permissible (Halal) for the Bank. Continuation of lease rentals in case of total loss or theft of vehicle If the leased vehicle is stolen or completely destroyed, the conventional leasing company continues charging the lease rent till the settlement of the Insurance claim. Under the Islamic system, rent  is consideration for usage of the leased asset, and if the asset has been stolen or destroyed, the concept of rental becomes void. As such, in the above-mentioned eventualities, Meezan bank does not charge the lease rental. – Sheikh Assim Al Hakeem

question: I have a garage; man comes to get his car repaired. It requires parts which I have to buy and this requires me to spend time, effort, transportation etc. So I tell him that the parts will cost him 1000 Dirhams, and he agrees – but I know that the parts will cost only 800 Dirhams. What is the ruling on the extra money that I charged him?
title: I have a garage; man comes to get his car repaired. It requires parts which I have to buy and this requires me to spend time, effort, transportation etc. So I tell him that the parts will cost him 1000 Dirhams, and he agrees – but I know that the parts will cost only 800 Dirhams. What is the ruling on the extra money that I charged him?
answer:
If you will charge 200 for fixing it, this is permissible. But if you are going to make a profit of the part itself, this is not permissible.

question: Here in India land BROKERS follow one technique. They make an arrangement with land owner. The contract format is like, the broker pay the owner (for example)10 million but he will sell to higher price according to his marketing skills. Brokers pay an advance of nominal amount and sell it to 3rd party with higher profit. Here the land owner gets lower amount and  does not know the real market value. Is this allowed?
title: Here in India land BROKERS follow one technique. They make an arrangement with land owner. The contract format is like, the broker pay the owner (for example)10 million but he will sell to higher price according to his marketing skills. Brokers pay an advance of nominal amount and sell it to 3rd party with higher profit. Here the land owner gets lower amount and  does not know the real market value. Is this allowed?
answer:
This is not permissible as the original seller should agree with them on a percentage or a fixed amount when the transaction takes place. If he knew how much profit they were making, he would not have approved it in the first place.

question: He is asking about Bank al-Jazeerah
title: He is asking about Bank al-Jazeerah
answer:
Is Bank al-Jazeerah in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia riba-based or Islamic?.
Praise be to Allaah.
Dr. Muhammad ibn Sa’ood al-‘Usaymi (may Allaah preserve him) was asked: What is the ruling on working in Bank al-Jazeerah? If I find another job, should I give up my job in Bank al-Jazeerah?
He replied: The basic principle is that it is permissible to work in Bank al-Jazeerah, because they seem to be striving to Islamize all their operations. But, by way of advice, I think that you should stipulate conditions for yourself that you will work in accordance with the decisions of the shar’i committee, and if you are forced to do some tasks that are not in accordance with their decisions, do not give up work immediately, rather inform the shar’i committee first, and seek their guidance. We and others are impatiently waiting for the Islamization of this bank to be completed. May Allaah help those in charge of it to do all that is good. And Allaah knows best. End quote.
http://www.halal2.com/ftawaDetail.asp?id=335
And Allaah knows best.
www.islamqa.com


                
                He is asking about Bank al-Jazeerah
        
        	            
			            Islamic economy |                                     February 10, 2014 8:14 pm
